+"""Daily transfer limits per customer, in minor units."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from bank.money import Money
+
+DEFAULT_DAILY_LIMIT_MINOR = 500_000  # 5,000.00 in a two-decimal currency
+
+
+class LimitExceeded(Exception):
+    """The transfer would take the day's total over the limit."""
+
+
+def remaining(sent_today: Money, limit: Money) -> Money:
+    """What the customer may still send today; never below zero."""
+    left = limit - sent_today
+    return left if left.minor > 0 else Money(0, limit.currency)
+
+
+def check(sent_today: Money, amount: Money, limit: Money) -> None:
+    """Raise ``LimitExceeded`` when ``amount`` does not fit in what is left of the limit."""
+    if amount.minor > remaining(sent_today, limit).minor:
+        raise LimitExceeded(f"{amount} is over the daily limit of {limit}")

+import pytest
+
+import bank.limits as limits
+from bank.money import Money
+
+
+def eur(text):
+    return Money.of(text, "EUR")
+
+
+def test_BENCH22_amount_within_the_limit_is_allowed():
+    limits.check(eur("100.00"), eur("50.00"), eur("200.00"))
+    limits.check(eur("150.00"), eur("50.00"), eur("200.00"))  # exactly the limit
+
+
+def test_BENCH22_amount_over_the_limit_is_refused():
+    with pytest.raises(limits.LimitExceeded):
+        limits.check(eur("150.00"), eur("50.01"), eur("200.00"))
+
+
+def test_BENCH22_remaining_never_goes_below_zero():
+    assert limits.remaining(eur("250.00"), eur("200.00")) == eur("0.00")
+    assert limits.remaining(eur("80.00"), eur("200.00")) == eur("120.00")
+
+
+def test_BENCH22_default_limit_is_five_thousand():
+    assert limits.DEFAULT_DAILY_LIMIT_MINOR == 500_000
